packages.label: מַרְקוּלִיס וְחִלּוּף הַכָּבוֹד
packages.label_en: The Idol of Desecration and Inversion of Honor
packages.reason: These four nodes are all expressions of the same essential reality: the desecration and inversion of Torah honor. שמרקולי"ס is the idolatrous stone-heap whose very name encodes the concept; מ"ר קלו"ס (= mar kilus) is the etymology — 'bitter shame,' i.e., the inversion of honor; חלוף הכבוד is the explicit concept name — 'substitution of honor'; כסיל and תלמיד שאינו הגון are the same type of person — the fool/unworthy recipient who embodies this inversion of Torah's honor when Torah is taught to him. The Rebbe explicitly identifies כסיל as the תלמיד שאינו הגון via the verse 'נוֹתֵן לִכְסִיל כָּבוֹד,' and identifies שמרקולי"ס as מ"ר קלו"ס as חלוף הכבוד. All five nodes share the same nature: they are forms and expressions of the anti-honor, the force that inverts and desecrates the holiness of Torah.

merge_notes.reason: This 2-node component is explicitly merged into Package 1 because the כסיל IS the תלמיד שאינו הגון — the Rebbe equates them via 'נוֹתֵן לִכְסִיל כָּבוֹד = לְתַלְמִיד שֶׁאֵינוֹ הָגוּן.' More critically, the כסיל as a type belongs to the same essential domain as שמרקולי"ס and חלוף הכבוד: all are expressions of the anti-honor force. The unworthy student is the human embodiment of מרקוליס — teaching Torah to him IS throwing Torah honor to the idol of desecration. The shared nature (not cause-effect) is the essential property of being the 'anti-honor,' whether expressed as an idol name, an etymology, a concept, or a person-type.

packages.label: מַלְכוּת וְגַדְלוּת
packages.reason: These two nodes are bechina-equivalent: 'מוֹסֶרְךָ לַמַּלְכוּת' means bringing R' Akiva into a state of 'גַּדְלוּת' (greatness). Malkhut in this context is not the political kingdom but the elevated spiritual state — gadlut — the state of spiritual greatness that enables and compels Torah revelation. Both nodes share the same essential nature: they describe the elevated, expansive state of mind and spiritual standing from which Torah can be revealed. The Rebbe equates the word 'malkhut' (as used by R' Shimon) with the concept of gadlut throughout the passage.

packages.label: מֶשִׁיכַת הָאֱלֹקוּת וּתְפִיסָה
packages.reason: These two nodes express the same essential reality from different angles: the drawing of Divine presence (אֱלֹקוּת) into the channels of the mind (רְהִיטֵי מֹחִין) through Torah IS a form of 'tephisa' — captivity, holding, containment. The Rebbe cites 'מֶלֶךְ אָסוּר בָּרְהָטִים — בְּרַהֲטֵי מֹחִין' to show that the Divine being drawn into the mind is inherently a bechina of tephisa. Both express the same phenomenon: the infinite held within the finite container of the mind. The Rebbe notes this is good and desirable to God even though it is a form of captivity. This is not cause-effect but two descriptions of the same event.
